Radiology Division | Antoni van Leeuwenhoek | 02 Jan 2025 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical Indication: Rising PSA (25.0 ng/mL) paired with an abnormal digital rectal examination; prior biopsy bucket Positive.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume registers at 31.91 mL. A discrete focus occupies the left peripheral zone spanning the base to mid-gland, spanning roughly 18 mm. T2 sequences show pronounced hypointensity with poorly demarcated borders. Diffusion-weighted imaging highlights restricted movement alongside low ADC mapping, pointing toward high cellular density. Post-contrast dynamics capture early, localized enhancement against the background parenchyma. No extraprostatic spread or seminal vesicle infiltration is seen. Pelvic nodes remain unenlarged. Skeletal survey reveals no suspicious osseous changes.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone (base/mid), measuring approximately 18 mm. Prostate volume 31.91 mL. PSA density 0.783 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.918368.

previous_notes.text: PSA values have climbed steadily, moving from 9.4 ng/mL in March 2022 up to 13.2 ng/mL by August 2023. Alongside an abnormal digital rectal examination and his continued work as an active dairy farmer, these markers prompted clinical attention. He remains otherwise stable.
